workload: Qwen3.5-0.8B, RTX 4060 Laptop SM89, vLLM 0.28.1, GPTQ-Marlin W4A16 backbone, tied BF16 lm_head, batch/concurrency 1

implementation.approximate_stage: Marlin W4 full-vocabulary scan selects top 128
implementation.rerank_stage: gather original BF16 rows, use torch.mv for M=1 and torch.bmm for M=2, then scatter exact shortlist scores
implementation.safety: disabled by default and shape/device guarded; unsupported shapes fall through to stock vLLM

conclusions: A quantized vLLM baseline is the fair control; replacing a BF16 baseline with W4 alone is not an agent-level win.
The GPTQ-Marlin backbone leaves the unquantized 248320x1024 tied output head as a residual bottleneck, so stock quantized vLLM is not locally optimal for this deployment point.
The candidate reproducibly improves bounded batch-1 greedy TPOT by about 1.55x and preserves all 768 tokens in the six-prompt throughput suite.

The 512-case GSM8K screen has identical aggregate accuracy but only 457 token-identical generations; therefore the candidate is an opt-in approximate mode, not a lossless replacement or proof of theoretical optimum.
